output.memo:
## Recommendation

Put the next quarter's effort into issue-usability ("Excessive ads and limited playback controls"). It ranks first, with a priority score of 37 [CL-004] and 15 complaints [CL-001]. It is also the first-ranked issue, so there is no competing recommendation to explain away.

The closest alternatives do not displace it. issue-other ranks second but is a general dissatisfaction bucket, so it points to no single piece of work. issue-playback has the highest severity among the larger issues but far fewer complaints.

## Supporting numbers

- issue-usability: 15 complaints [CL-001], severity sum 37 [CL-002], mean severity 2.466667 [CL-003], priority score 37 [CL-004].
- issue-other: priority score 31 [CL-008] from 15 complaints [CL-005].
- issue-playback: priority score 25 [CL-012] from 7 complaints [CL-009], mean severity 3.571429 [CL-011].

## Alternatives

- issue-other (rank 2): severity sum 31 [CL-006], mean severity 2.066667 [CL-007]. It is a catch-all, so it is hard to act on. It would only change the recommendation if a clearer theme emerged from it.
- issue-playback (rank 3): app crashes, loading failures and connectivity problems. Its mean severity is 3.571429 [CL-011], well above issue-usability's. If stability matters more to you than the volume of complaints, this is the strongest alternative.
- issue-billing (rank 4): restricted playback controls for non-premium users. It has 6 complaints [CL-013] and a priority score of 17 [CL-016]. It overlaps in subject with issue-usability, so the two could be scoped together.
- issue-access has a mean severity of 4.000000 [CL-023] but only 2 complaints [CL-021]. That is too few to base a quarter's effort on, though the issue may deserve a quick look.

## Representative reviews

These are among the most severe examples plus a few picked by hash. They are not typical.

- issue-usability: "We can't even go back few second to play music?" [review:9e5f9745-f8be-48d3-b9de-4d118507d94a]
- issue-usability: "The ads are so loud :'(" [review:ab67a772-c3b7-42ba-9b80-8d21d3857018]
- issue-playback: "App is stuck on loading/logo screen" [review:66a29b3c-c14d-440e-b722-b23e0c99ae82]
- issue-billing: "The ability to skip a song or go to previous song has been removed from non subscribed users." [review:a3605554-5c3a-441d-836e-e9fdea83eb2e]

## Limits

- The labels come from a model and were checked against only a small hand-labeled set.
- The quote and the topic come from separate questions and can point at different sentences.
- Each issue is a whole topic, not a single defect.
- Agreement between the two engines is not accuracy.
- The quotes are the most severe examples and a few picked by hash, not typical ones.
- Of 100 completed reviews, 27 were flagged for review (27.0 percent), so some labels may change on a closer look.
- These numbers show how often and how severely topics came up. They cannot show why.

## Recommendation

Put the next quarter's effort into issue-usability ("Excessive ads and limited playback controls"). It ranks first, with a priority score of 37 [CL-004] and 15 complaints [CL-001]. It is also the first-ranked issue, so there is no competing recommendation to explain away.

The closest alternatives do not displace it. issue-other ranks second but is a general dissatisfaction bucket, so it points to no single piece of work. issue-playback has the highest severity among the larger issues but far fewer complaints.

## Supporting numbers

- issue-usability: 15 complaints [CL-001], severity sum 37 [CL-002], mean severity 2.466667 [CL-003], priority score 37 [CL-004].
- issue-other: priority score 31 [CL-008] from 15 complaints [CL-005].
- issue-playback: priority score 25 [CL-012] from 7 complaints [CL-009], mean severity 3.571429 [CL-011].

## Alternatives

- issue-other (rank 2): severity sum 31 [CL-006], mean severity 2.066667 [CL-007]. It is a catch-all, so it is hard to act on. It would only change the recommendation if a clearer theme emerged from it.
- issue-playback (rank 3): app crashes, loading failures and connectivity problems. Its mean severity is 3.571429 [CL-011], well above issue-usability's. If stability matters more to you than the volume of complaints, this is the strongest alternative.
- issue-billing (rank 4): restricted playback controls for non-premium users. It has 6 complaints [CL-013] and a priority score of 17 [CL-016]. It overlaps in subject with issue-usability, so the two could be scoped together.
- issue-access has a mean severity of 4.000000 [CL-023] but only 2 complaints [CL-021]. That is too few to base a quarter's effort on, though the issue may deserve a quick look.

## Representative reviews

These are among the most severe examples plus a few picked by hash. They are not typical.

## Limits

- The labels come from a model and were checked against only a small hand-labeled set.
- The quote and the topic come from separate questions and can point at different sentences.
- Each issue is a whole topic, not a single defect.
- Agreement between the two engines is not accuracy.
